sources.title: Human History Map civilization index
sources.note: Exact Pratiharas identity, approximate 1000 to 1200 interval and separately indexed neighboring, predecessor and successor-like records.

sources.title: Human History Map 700 CE borders
sources.note: Decoded pre-imperial snapshot proving the exact target is absent and documenting earlier ownership of tested north Indian centers.

sources.title: Human History Map 800 CE borders
sources.note: Decoded separately indexed gurjara-pratihara geometry and named point ownership before the target interval.

sources.title: Human History Map 900 CE borders
sources.note: Decoded second gurjara-pratihara snapshot and simultaneous Chauhan, Pala, Shahi and other layers.

sources.title: Human History Map 1000 CE borders
sources.note: Decoded first exact Pratiharas geometry, coordinate hash, topology, point tests and overlaps with Rajput kingdoms and Palas.

sources.title: Human History Map 1100 CE borders
sources.note: Decoded second exact Pratiharas geometry, coordinate hash and implausible exclusion of Kannauj and other secure political centers.

sources.title: Human History Map 1200 CE borders
sources.note: Decoded disappearance of the exact target and broad replacement by Delhi Sultanate and Rajput kingdoms layers.

sources.title: Human History Map 1279 CE borders
sources.note: Decoded later Delhi Sultanate and minor Hindu kingdoms assignments used only as atlas continuity context.

sources.title: Tamil Nadu Open University, History of India up to 1206 CE
sources.note: Official university synthesis of the Gurjara-Pratihara rise, Kannauj phase, political contraction and early eleventh-century ending.

sources.title: IGNOU, Early Medieval Polities in North India, seventh to thirteenth centuries
sources.note: University unit treating Gurjara-Pratihara power, regional lords, Kannauj and the changing political landscape after imperial contraction.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India library, The Age of Imperial Kanauj: Rise and Fall of the Pratihara Empire
sources.note: Scholarly reconstruction of rulers, campaigns, disputed dates, Kannauj politics and the uncertain final Pratihara sequence.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India library, Dynasties of Northern India: Pratihara origins and early power
sources.note: Scholarly discussion of Mandor, Avanti, Kannauj and the dynastic origin traditions, with warnings against literal noble pedigrees.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India library, History of the Chandellas
sources.note: Scholarly reconstruction of Rajyapala, the 1018 Kannauj raid, the Chandela response and Vidyadhara-era political change.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India, Archaeological Museum and Monuments at Sarnath
sources.note: Official site history placing Pratihara collapse before Kalachuri and Gahadavala control in the middle Ganges region.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India library, History of the Gahadavalas
sources.note: Scholarly account of Chandradeva and the distinct Gahadavala dynasty that rose around Kannauj after Pratihara and Kalachuri competition.

sources.title: Indian Antiquary XVIII, copper-plate grant of Trilochanapala, Vikrama year 1084
sources.note: Primary scholarly edition, estampage-based text and summary of the 1027 Sanskrit Nagari grant found at Jhusi.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey Lists, North-Western Provinces: Jhusi
sources.note: Official archaeological list locating Jhusi opposite Prayaga and recording the discovered Trilochanapala copper plate, fort mound, tank and wells.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India Memoir 60, Kausambi
sources.note: Official ASI memoir describing the 1036 Kara inscription, village grant in Kausambi-mandala and conventional identification of Yashapala.

sources.title: Sanjay Sharma, Negotiating Identity and Status under the Gurjara-Pratiharas of Kanauj
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study of royal and subordinate status, land gifts, temples and changing political relationships under Pratihara rule.

sources.title: Shanta Rani Sharma, Exploding the Myth of the Gurjara Identity of the Imperial Pratiharas
sources.note: Peer-reviewed reassessment of origin labels and the danger of turning later identity arguments into simple ethnic facts.

sources.title: Epigraphia Indica I, Vaillabhattasvamin temple inscriptions at Gwalior
sources.note: Primary edition of the 876 endowment naming fields, cultivators, oil workers, lamps, garlands, measurements and temple support.

sources.title: University of St Andrews MacTutor, A history of zero
sources.note: Academic mathematics history explaining the dated Gwalior inscription and its written zeros in practical measurements and offerings.

sources.title: Haryana Tourism, Vishvamitra Ka Tila at Pehowa
sources.note: Official heritage account of the 882 merchant contribution inscription, brick temple plinth and epic-story sculptures.

sources.title: Siddham INIG932, Gwalior Fort inscription of Vikrama year 932
sources.note: Scholarly digital record connecting officer Alla, Mihira Bhoja and the rock-cut Caturbhuj temple at Gwalior.

sources.title: Siddham INIG933, Gwalior Fort inscription of Vikrama year 933
sources.note: Scholarly record and script metadata for the Sanskrit Siddhamatrika endowment associated with Gwalior temple support.

sources.title: Siddham INIG999, Rakhetra inscription of Vikrama year 999
sources.note: Scholarly digital record of Vinayakapala-era irrigation work, a river setting and the named writer Bhailadaman.

sources.title: INFLIBNET, Rajashekhara and Indian Poetics
sources.note: University account of poet training, Avantisundari, literary criticism, court service and an ideal daily routine for writers.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum, Four-armed goddess, probably Gauri
sources.note: Museum record for a tenth-century central Indian sculpture with goddess, Ganesha, animal mount and probable women donors.

sources.title: IGNOU, Organisation of Agricultural and Craft Production in early medieval North India
sources.note: University synthesis of crops, irrigation, craft production, labor and ecological variation in early medieval northern India.

sources.title: IGNOU, Agrarian society and stratification in early medieval North India
sources.note: University unit on peasants, landholders, labor obligations, social hierarchy and regional variation from 550 to 1300.

sources.title: IGNOU, Trade, trading networks and urbanisation in North India, 300 to 1300
sources.note: University synthesis of merchants, routes, markets, guilds, taxes and the debated scale of early medieval urban change.

sources.title: IGNOU, Castes, Gender and Professions in early medieval India
sources.note: University unit on jati, work, gender hierarchy, social mobility, Sanskrit learning and the limits of elite normative texts.

sources.title: IGNOU, Science and learning in early medieval India
sources.note: University course material on mathematics, astronomy, medical writing, metallurgy and technical learning across the early medieval period.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India library, Temples of North India
sources.note: Authoritative architectural survey of Pratihara-style temples, Gwalior, Bateshwar, Amrol, plans, stone carving and sculptural programs.

sources.title: Puratattva, Anai: A Settlement in the Varuna Region
sources.note: Archaeological report on a 700 to 1000 middle-Ganges mud house, ovens, pottery, bangles, tools, cowries, wells and evidence limits.

sources.title: Anatomy in ancient India: a focus on the Susruta Samhita
sources.note: Peer-reviewed medical history of anatomical, surgical and teacher-pupil traditions, with debated textual chronology and no local-clinic claim.

sources.title: British Museum, Gurjara-Pratihara coin and imitation
sources.note: Museum catalogue for a debased silver Indo-Sasanian imitation with ruler bust, fire altar, attendant, size and weight.

sources.title: British Museum, Gurjara-Pratihara-style sandstone goddess
sources.note: Museum catalogue for a tenth-century Malwa sandstone deity, material, dimensions and religious interpretation.

sources.title: IGNOU, Culture in the post-Gupta period
sources.note: University survey of growing temples, Shaiva, Vaishnava, goddess, Buddhist and Jain traditions, literature and artistic change.

sources.title: Monica L. Smith, Territories, corridors, and networks
sources.note: Archaeological model explaining why premodern states often worked through nodes, routes and uneven influence rather than surveyed borders.

proposedOverrides.summary: The last Kannauj Pratiharas and their long afterlife, separated from an atlas polygon that stretches two centuries and misses the imperial core.

batchIdentityNotes: Exact target pratiharas is indexed approximately 1000 to 1200 CE and was missing both a card and a researched override at initial audit.
The separately carded gurjara-pratihara record covers 800 to 1000 and remains untouched. The new target records it only as a predecessor, never as an alias.
Only world-1000 and world-1100 contain the exact target. It is absent at 700, 800, 900, 1200, 1279 and 1300.
The 1000 target is one Polygon, one ring and 29 positions with SHA-256 610039ec6650844e94ac104e78125ae6df7620a406eca047ffb2bc94e7f416b3.
The 1100 target is one Polygon, one ring and 31 positions with SHA-256 936e72e00c7635bc64be188b5fa2fc5341c63ab8bc0e16884b5e0d7958d1959f.
Both target polygons include Ayodhya, Gorakhpur and Patna but exclude Kannauj, Gwalior, Prayaga, Jhusi, Kara, Kausambi, western centers and the earlier Mandor region.
At 1000 the target overlaps rajput-kingdoms at Ayodhya and Gorakhpur and palas at Patna. At 1100 it implausibly owns Patna while excluding the secure last-Pratihara grant sites.
The card ends the historical polity around 1036, sets fell to 1036, leaves successors empty and treats 1036 to 1200 as atlas afterlife rather than continuous rule.
No appliesTo alias is added. Separate Rajput, Chauhan, Chandela, Pala, Ghaznavid, Solanki and other cards and overrides remain untouched.
